faq.q: Which regex flags and features does it support?
faq.a: All six JavaScript flags via checkboxes: g (global), i (case-insensitive), m (multiline), s (dotall), u (unicode) and y (sticky). It shows live highlighting of matches, a match count, and per-match details including every capturing group by number and named groups like (?<name>). A Replace tab supports $1, $2 and $<name> references with live preview.

Yes, 17 presets, each with a sample test string: email, Indian mobile, Indian PIN code, PAN card, Aadhaar, GSTIN, IFSC code, URL, IPv4, date dd/mm/yyyy, time, hex colour, username, strong password, HTML tag, whitespace and duplicate words. A collapsible cheatsheet covers character classes, quantifiers, anchors, groups, lookarounds and escapes.

faq.q: Does it warn about common regex mistakes?
faq.a: Yes — a feature most testers lack. Beyond reporting syntax errors, it flags patterns that are valid but likely to surprise you: a dot not crossing newlines without the s flag, ^/$ anchoring to the whole string without m, only the first match without g, nested quantifiers that risk catastrophic backtracking, a literal dot inside a character class, and \d/\w matching ASCII only under the u flag.

Yes. Your pattern, test string, replacement and flags are saved locally so they survive a reload. Patterns that actually matched something are kept in a history list (up to 10) you can reload with one click. Press Ctrl/Cmd+Enter or R to re-run. Everything runs in your browser with no server component.
